# AI Media Scout — 2026-11-08

Today’s expanded edition covers 92 creative fields, adding game localization and stage lighting, with 789 configured repository queries and 22 model tasks. It contains 51 detailed guides and 185 additional eligible, license-screened discoveries awaiting full profiles. Sixteen guides complete earlier screened entries. Discovery includes recent, newly created and established work; there is no popularity cutoff or daily count quota. Current retained-catalog metadata, 1,187 additional repositories from today’s query union, 535 license-bearing metadata records and targeted source follow-ups were screened beyond the automatic README shortlist. Raw unreviewed and excluded candidates remain local; this is not a claim that every collected candidate was fully reviewed. All featured software grants were reviewed in full, with model weights, fonts/assets, paid services and required proprietary hosts separated. Every item has a dated assessment of licensing, results, setup, maintenance, independent use and dependencies. Unresolved evidence stays Quality unverified; explicit current prototype/instability reasons alone support Experimental. No discovered tool was installed/run, and no new tool is recommended merely for its stars, documentation, test totals or owner demo. Existing weekly library coverage was complete before collection; the new source reviews join that week and will be rechecked in the cumulative library. Verified collection: 789/789 repository queries attempted; 789 successful, 0 partial, 0 failed and 126 bounded/truncated. All 22 model tasks were attempted; 0 failed. These are bounded discovery attempts, not an exhaustive census or quality approval. Separate from successful search queries, 39 watchlist fetches and 3 enrichment attempts failed; the detailed warnings remain in the report. A 404/409 is an availability gap, not proof of abandonment or license revocation.

Documentation reviewed today. Tools are not hands-on tested unless explicitly stated. Requirements and performance remain source-specific.

## Search and review counts

92 creative fields; 789/789 repository queries attempted; 22/22 model-task queries attempted. 30925 distinct source candidates and 918 model leads. 51 detailed profiles and 185 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 0 partial repository queries, 126 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 2 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

## Research beyond GitHub

- **gitlab** · searched: Current primary captures for AudioStellar, perso-ai, LibreTerrain and Embedded Amp Model were inspected/compared and remain unchanged. Bounded live GitLab discovery found MotionNet material describing an extensive proposed architecture, but no full license/implemented release was established; it stays local. No unchanged tool is re-featured as new. [Source](https://gitlab.com/ayrsd/audiostellar/-/raw/audiostellar2/README.md) [Source](https://gitlab.com/algomus.fr/perso-ai/-/raw/master/README.md) [Source](https://gitlab.com/libreterrain/libreterrain/-/raw/main/README.md) [Source](https://gitlab.com/ar39907/embedded-amp-model/-/raw/main/README.md)
- **codeberg** · gap: Current live discovery requests returned non-retryable robots/access restrictions. No alternate route bypassed them and no new eligible current code/license review was established. This is an access gap, not a claim that no creative AI project exists there.
- **sourcehut** · gap: Current live SourceHut discovery was blocked by robots/access restrictions. No alternate route bypassed that restriction; current creative-AI software and full grants remain unverified for this source group.
- **packages** · searched: Live PyPI JSON established game-localizer and gameloc package metadata and official source links; their source/license/workflows were separately reviewed. NuGet TensorStack registry context was checked. HTML challenge pages are not package documentation, and the current mediakit-mcp PyPI request returned 404; that installation gap is disclosed in its full guide. [Source](https://pypi.org/pypi/game-localizer/json) [Source](https://pypi.org/pypi/gameloc/json) [Source](https://pypi.org/pypi/mediakit-mcp/json)
- **creative-plugins** · searched: Current primary creative-host/plugin sources include Krita, Blender, Godot, ComfyUI, Resolve, Adobe and game/lighting integrations. The Blender Formula-to-Nodes listing/version history demonstrates an AI/MCP role, but the complete official software-license fetch returned 404, so it is held rather than admitted on a listing badge. Required proprietary hosts and restricted models are labeled separately. [Source](https://extensions.blender.org/add-ons/formula-to-nodes/)
- **project-sites** · searched: All 92 observed fields received a live primary web-source attempt beyond GitHub: 98 unique URLs, 97 HTTP successes and one SSL failure; three PDFs were bounded to 2 MB. Script/navigation shells and blocked full-paper requests remain explicit gaps. Readable site context was inspected; a successful HTTP response is not a complete source review, exhaustive web census or implementation/quality approval. [Source](https://abdallah28r.github.io/taarib/en/) [Source](https://lacylights.com/) [Source](https://shopprentice.com/)
- **research-code** · searched: Research-code review spans controlled relighting, image-edit evaluation, MIDI composition, medical-volume visualization, fMRI reconstruction and neural codecs. Complete software grants were checked separately from datasets/models. Primary comparison-paper search excerpts document scoped DiLightNet research use, but full current CVF paper fetches returned 403 and were not bypassed. Owner metrics or paper provenance alone never grant a Recommended label. [Source](https://dilightnet.github.io/) [Source](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2025/papers/Litman_LightSwitch_Multi-view_Relighting_with_Material-guided_Diffusion_ICCV_2025_paper.pdf)
- **international** · searched: Live primary multilingual sources include Arabic/RTL localization, Japanese/Korean game and creative workflows, Chinese agent-media pipelines, Persian typography/translation, Thai localization QA, Vietnamese subtitles/animation and Portuguese transcription. Every selected tool still needs a concrete creative AI role and complete software grant; language and research origin do not determine quality. [Source](https://abdallah28r.github.io/taarib/en/) [Source](https://github.com/akin-demir/arabic-calligraphy-skill) [Source](https://github.com/arqhive/game-korean-localization-pipeline)

## HDify

Images & design · Photography, restoration & color · Browser tools & web media

The repository was created on 2026-11-07. This is its first full guide in this library, not independent validation of a new release.

### Quality assessment: Quality unverified

The current software grant and concrete creative AI role are supported. Scoped source, setup, support, output and dependency checks leave unresolved evidence gaps; a recommendation is not established.

Scope: Private photo-upscaling studies with an adjustable restoration strength and a direct before/after comparison.

Evidence checked: 2026-11-08. No local execution implied.

- **Open-source software license · verified:** The complete root software license was read and archived. The grant covers this project code; unresolved model, service and asset terms are disclosed separately. [Source](https://github.com/Dhee2211/HDify/blob/main/LICENSE)
- **Creative results · documented:** Owner examples compare reduced source images with 4× reconstructions. The linked app was not accessible through the web-fetch tool in this review, so no live app test is claimed. [Source](https://github.com/Dhee2211/HDify/blob/main/README.md) [Source](https://github.com/Dhee2211/HDify/blob/main/NOTICE.md)
- **Reproducible setup · documented:** Use a recent compatible browser and serve the cloned static files over local HTTP. There is no application build/backend dependency; model downloads are separate. Independent reproduction has not been established in this review.
```sh
git clone https://github.com/sandraschi/avatar-mcp
```


```sh
cd avatar-mcp
```


```sh
uv sync --all-extras
```


```sh
uv run python -m avatar_mcp.server
```

4. Compare the rendered result and state read-backs before using the full timeline; stop the stack with stop-resolve-ai.sh.
### Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [Source 1](https://github.com/willturner-maker/resolve-ai-workflow/blob/main/README.md)

- **Hardware:** Maintainer recommends at least 48 GB unified memory, tuned on a 96 GB Mac. The initial language-model download is tens of GB; optional vision adds roughly 560 MB of environment and 52 MB of models. These are documented recommendations/sizes, not tested minima.
- **Software:** macOS/Homebrew, Python 3.11+, Node 20+, Apple Silicon, Resolve Studio, local Splash model server and Blender for the title path. Optional vision uses its own Python 3.12 environment.
- **Platforms:** Apple Silicon macOS workstation. Other OS and Intel Mac routes are not documented as equivalent.

### License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [Source 1](https://github.com/willturner-maker/resolve-ai-workflow/blob/main/LICENSE) [Source 2](https://github.com/willturner-maker/resolve-ai-workflow/blob/main/README.md)

- **Code:** MIT
- **Weights:** MIT orchestration scripts; Resolve Studio, Claude Code, individual MCP components, Blender and model weights have separate terms. Optional YuNet/SFace grants are identified, but the maintainer flags unclear hosted MediaPipe model terms.
- **Commercial:** Software use follows MIT. MIT orchestration scripts; Resolve Studio, Claude Code, individual MCP components, Blender and model weights have separate terms. Optional YuNet/SFace grants are identified, but the maintainer flags unclear hosted MediaPipe model terms.

### Demo & examples

The owner publishes frame/filmstrip examples and benchmark boundaries. A critic pass is model feedback, not human quality approval or proof that every requirement was captured. [Source 1](https://github.com/mirac221/frame-judge/blob/main/README.md)

### Install

Clone the source and review/run its installer for the supported agent hosts. Prepare Node, FFmpeg, a vision-capable model and, for web capture, an installed compatible browser or Playwright. [Source 1](https://github.com/mirac221/frame-judge/blob/main/README.md)

1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
2. Clone the source and review/run its installer for the supported agent hosts. Prepare Node, FFmpeg, a vision-capable model and, for web capture, an installed compatible browser or Playwright.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mirac221/frame-judge
```


```sh
node frame-judge/scripts/install.mjs
```


```sh
cd frame-judge
```


```sh
node scripts/judge.mjs doctor
```

### First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [Source 1](https://github.com/mirac221/frame-judge/blob/main/README.md)

1. Give the builder a concrete visual brief and produce a real render.
2. Capture representative devices/times or filmstrips and give the separate critic the brief and images.
3. Review complaints tied to actual frames, fix them and compare another capture.
4. Inspect the final artifact yourself; keep relay/manual review routes distinct from tested local integrations.
### Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [Source 1](https://github.com/mirac221/frame-judge/blob/main/README.md)

- **Hardware:** Minimum system RAM, VRAM and total disk space are not documented in the reviewed instructions.
- **Software:** Node 18+, FFmpeg and an image-capable AI model. Website capture uses Chrome/Edge/Chromium with Node 22+, or Playwright.
- **Platforms:** Agent/browser-dependent. Claude Code and Antigravity routes are marked tested by the maintainer; several other named clients are documentation-derived routes.

- **Commercial:** Software use follows Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 code with LICENSE/NOTICE preservation. Agent/vision model service, browser and your input media have separate terms.

1. Open 127.0.0.1:9010 and inspect the synthetic demo first, keeping it distinct from inference.

3. Review/correct the masks in linked slices and 3D view.
4. Export visual views/PNG/offline HTML with required notices; keep patient data out of public examples.

A local MCP image server lets an AI agent execute explicit image conversions, crops, metadata removal, contact-style merges and thumbnails through a structured tool interface. Blocked captions can reduce a summary to description-only input; automatically sampled frames can be blank/intros. This is a media-research aid, not an image-generation tool or factual authenticity guarantee. Bundled Instrument Serif is OFL; optional SponsorBlock data has separate community database terms. Neither is relicensed by the extension MIT grant. [Source 1](https://github.com/sub8u/honest-thumbnails/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/sub8u/honest-thumbnails/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)

### Get the tool

- [Repository](https://github.com/sub8u/honest-thumbnails)
- [Documentation](https://github.com/sub8u/honest-thumbnails/blob/main/README.md)
